chapter: Horace Henderson band and Roy Eldridge
title: Sent for by Jimmy Smith's Missourians to play the Savoy
summary: About 1932 he was sent for to play two weeks at the Savoy with the Missourians, part of which had split off when Cab was put in front; a tape break and false start follow.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: All six of you working together all that time?
Yeah, uh-huh. Never went anyplace. So a guy sent for me to come down here, named Jimmy Smith.

He had a band, the Missourians, and it was all with Cab, and Cab -- so half of them decided to go out, because they put Cab in front of this band, and I think some of them didn't like it so well, because they was already organized. Then they were -- they was organizing their own band, so I come down in about 1932, to play -- they sent for me to come down and play at the Savoy. They were in the Savoy. Danny ______ Dixon was on trumpet, and Ted, and we played the Savoy for about two weeks.
Well, wait a minute. You're going too fast. Wait a minute. We'll just finish this off, so we can get started on the other one right.
Well, I wanted to -- I just want to -- we mustn't forget where we were, but --
One, two, three. I think we were there with the band and --
